# Isle of Arran UNESCO Geopark

From volcanic eruptions to glacial landscapes, discover the wildlife, biodiversity, and archaeological heritage.

## Isle of Arran Geopark at a glance

- Archaeological sites:
Machrie Moor Standing Stones, 28 chambered cairns, cursus monument at Drumadoon

- Nature & outdoors:
Brodick Bay, Kildonan Bay, Goatfell

- Towns & villages:
Brodick, Lamlash, Lochranza


Map of Scotland

## Plan your Arran adventure

Soak up views from the island's highest peaks, feel the sea breeze as you cycle Arran's scenic coastal route, discover some of the island's most popular attractions, or step back thousands of years at its remarkable prehistoric sites.

### Hiking and walking

Known as "Scotland in Miniature", Arran is a paradise for hillwalkers. Tackle Goatfell, the island's highest peak, and breathe in the fresh air from above, or explore the rugged ridge routes of the northern mountains, including Cìr Mhòr and Beinn Tarsuinn.

[Find more about walking and hiking on Arran](https://www.visitarran.com/see-do/activities/walking)

### Arran Coastal Way

Cycle the iconic 65-mile Arran Coastal Way around the island, stopping at picturesque villages, beaches, local attractions, and cafés along the route. Whether you choose to complete the full route or explore shorter sections, there are plenty of scenic detours, hidden gems, and exciting experiences to discover across the island.

[Explore the Arran Coastal Way](https://www.coastalway.co.uk/)

### Brodick Castle and Country Park

One of Arran's most popular attractions, Brodick Castle offers a fascinating glimpse into the island's history, surrounded by woodland walks, formal gardens, and scenic views across Brodick Bay.

[Visit Brodick Castle, Garden & Country Park](https://www.nts.org.uk/visit/places/brodick-castle)

### Machrie Moor Standing Stones

Step back in time at one of Scotland's prehistoric sites. Set amid a spectacular island scenery, these mysterious stone circles, standing stones, burial cairns and cists are among Arran's most significant archaeological treasures, offering a fascinating glimpse into the island's ancient past.

[Immerse yourself in history at Machrie Moor Standing Stones](https://www.historicenvironment.scot/visit/all/machrie-moor-standing-stones/)

### The Arran Trust

Arran is committed to protecting its unique natural and cultural heritage. Visitors can support through the Arran Trust, a charity that funds conservation, environmental and heritage projects.

[Find out more about the Arran Trust](https://www.visitarran.com/the-arran-trust)

## Arran by area

From bustling coastal villages and picturesque harbours to peaceful beaches and historic landmarks, each corner of Arran has its own unique character.

[Brodick](https://ayrshireandarran.com/broddick/) \- This bustling port is the largest on Arran. Home to the peak of Goatfell, delicious eateries, and 18-hole golf course and much more to explore.

[Lamlash](https://www.lamlasharran.co.uk/) \- The most populated village on Arran boasts spectacular views out to the Holy Isle and great opportunities for sailing and boat trips.

[Holy Isle](https://holyisle.org/) \- Visible across Lamlash Bay, Holy Isle is renowned for its spiritual heritage, wildlife, and remarkable geological features, making it a key part of the Arran Geopark experience.

[Whiting Bay](https://ayrshireandarran.com/whiting-bay/) \- A popular tourist village located on the southern half of Arran, combining the best of modern and historical Scotland.

[Kildonan](https://ayrshireandarran.com/kildonan/) – A small village situated on the southern coast of Arran. Its main attractions include Kildonan Beach and castle ruins.

[Kilmory](https://ayrshireandarran.com/kilmory/) \- Kilmory is a small village on the south coast of Arran, between Lagg and Kildonan. Here you can explore its enchanting woods with the Fairy Garden Trail.

[Find out more about the Isle of Arran Geopark](https://www.arran-geopark.org.uk/)

## Plan your trip to Isle of Arran Geopark

There are three options to travel to Arran. All involve catching a ferry, as there’s no bridge!

- Getting there
- Accessibility

### Getting there

Ferry

## Ferry

You can travel from Ardrossan Harbour or from Troon Harbour to Brodick. An alternative ferry route is via Argyll from Claonaig to Lochranza. It’s recommended that you book ferry tickets in advance at all times of the year, as services can be very busy. You can bring your car on all these ferries, too.

[Find out more information on ferries to Arran](https://www.calmac.co.uk/en-gb/timetables/#/firth_of_clyde)

Once you’re on the island, there are regular bus services from Brodick to all the island’s villages.

* * *

Train

## Train

There are direct train services between Glasgow Central and Ardrossan Harbour. You can also catch a train to Troon, where a bus service takes you to the harbour.

* * *

Driving

## Driving

Although Arran is an island, it is easily accessible from Glasgow and it doesn’t take long to reach at all. Ferries also run frequently throughout the year.

Typical journey times by car to the harbours at Ardrossan and Troon are:

- Glasgow – about 45 minutes
- Edinburgh – about 2 hours
- London – about 7.5 hours

If you are bringing a car over to the island, you must book in advance.

* * *

### Accessibility

Arran offers a range of accessible accommodation, attractions, and experiences available across the island. When booking your stay, check individual accommodation listings for accessibility information and facilities. Public toilets can be found in several locations across the island, including Brodick, Lamlash, Whiting Bay, Kildonan, Kilmory, Blackwaterfoot, Lochranza, Corrie and Sannox.

## FAQs

What is a Geopark?

### What is a Geopark?

[UNESCO Global Geoparks](https://www.visitscotland.com/places-to-go/unesco/geoparks) are areas of international geological significance that use their natural and cultural heritage to promote conservation, education, and sustainable development. Rather than focusing solely on protecting important geological sites, Geoparks work with local communities, businesses, and organisations to celebrate their unique landscapes while supporting sustainable tourism and local economies.

* * *

When is the best time to visit the Isle of Arran Geopark?

### When is the best time to visit the Isle of Arran Geopark?

The Isle of Arran UNESCO Global Geopark can be enjoyed throughout the year, with each season offering a unique perspective on the island's landscapes and heritage. During spring and summer, longer days provide the perfect opportunity to explore Arran's mountains, coastal trails, geological sites, and ancient monuments, while wildlife enthusiasts can spot seabirds, seals, and red deer across the island.

In autumn, the changing colours transform Arran's forests and glens, creating spectacular scenery for walking and photography. Winter offers a quieter experience, with dramatic coastal views, cosy cafés, local distilleries, and clear nights that are ideal for stargazing.

* * *

How long should I stay in the Isle of Arran Geopark?

### How long should I stay in the Isle of Arran Geopark?

While it's possible to experience some of Arran's highlights in a day, we recommend spending at least two to three days to fully appreciate the Isle of Arran UNESCO Global Geopark. With 600 million years of geological history, stunning coastal landscapes, mountain trails, ancient monuments, and charming villages to explore, there's plenty to fill a longer stay. A week on Arran allows you to discover the island at a slower pace, whether you're hiking Goatfell, visiting Machrie Moor Standing Stones, exploring the coastline, or enjoying local food and drink.

* * *

Where can I stay in the Isle of Arran Geopark?

### Where can I stay in the Isle of Arran Geopark?

Whether you're looking for a cosy B&B, a self-catering cottage, a seaside guesthouse, or a campsite surrounded by nature, the Isle of Arran Geopark offers accommodation to suit every style and budget.

[Find your perfect Arran accommodation](https://www.visitarran.com/stay)
